record.file_problem: Repository record contains the README and file list only; the referenced reports and result files were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a multi-feature, multi-site decomposition of refusal-related features, refining the single-direction account with a different method. It does not report the original difference-in-means ablation or addition tests.
record.gate_note: The README reports summary findings about SAE features and causal steering. It does not describe the steering protocol or what qualified a feature as passing. The 0.94 detection score concerns automated descriptions, not a claim-version outcome, so it is not recorded as a row. File names and the existence of result files are not treated as inspected results.
record.test_reason: The study asks whether refusal in Gemma 3 12B splits into several domain-specific SAE features. That question bears on V4, refusal as more than one direction. Only the causal steering result could show it, and the README gives no outcome measure for it. The full results (findings/rq1_poc_results.md, data/milestone_5_results) were not read, so no verdict can be drawn yet.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README reports refusal-relevant SAE features with distinct site roles: general intent at the prompt, domain-specific expression in the response. It reports a critical width transition at 65k and says 8/8 selected features pass causal steering. It frames the work as a Master's thesis proof of concept.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Matryoshka sparse autoencoders and feature steering to study refusal-feature decomposition, rather than the original difference-in-means direction and its ablation/addition tests. This is a thesis proof-of-concept repository, not a reported reproduction of the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports a width transition at 16k → 65k and distinguishes last-prompt-token from mean-response-token sites; steering is reported at layer 36 (75% depth).

fits_no_version.finding: Contrastive SAE activation analysis finds 102 refusal-relevant features in 6 sub-types. A general intent feature sits at the last prompt token, and 43 domain-specific expression features sit at mean response tokens. Most gains come at the 16k→65k width step.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-associated SAE features in an instruct model split into a general prompt-side intent feature and domain-specific response-side expression features, and the split depends on SAE width.

record.problems: The README is a summary of a Master's thesis proof of concept. It does not provide the underlying metrics, prompt details, baselines, uncertainty, controls, or the causal-steering pass criterion; referenced reports and results were not inspected.
record.rows_left_out: No separate result rows were left out. The README's 0.94 detection score is not a direct outcome on a listed claim version.

No reported comparison with a single direction. No affine, cone or dominant-plus-others geometry. No refusal-rate effect of steering individual or multiple features in the README.
Separate encoding of harmfulness and refusal. The intent-vs-expression site split is suggestive, but no harm-judgment measure is reported.
Transfer across languages, variants, or base to instruct.
Effect of training method or timing.

missing.what: Steering outcome per feature (refusal rate or score change, coefficients, baseline, pass criterion), which could bear on V4.
Cosine similarity between site features or domain features, and any comparison with a difference-in-means direction (working_notes/research_arditi.md suggests one may exist).

record.verdict_notes: README-only reading. The feature counts are SAE decompositions; SAEs split any concept at larger widths, so the counts alone do not bear on V4. Verdicts withheld until the steering results file is read. The 0.94 detection score correctly has no row.

versions.untested_parts: Difference-in-means direction, all-layer/position ablation, refusal induction by adding the direction, and retained general capabilities.
Jailbreak suppression of the direction and robustness training against its ablation.
The README does not compare affine, cone, and dominant-direction accounts, establish independent residual-stream directions, or report a direct comparison against the single-direction method.
Separate encoding of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Effects of refusal-training method or timing.

relation.reason: The README asks whether refusal in Gemma 3 12B splits into domain-specific SAE features, the same topic as V4. It never mentions the difference-in-means direction or its ablation, and its reported results cannot show whether a version holds. The file list includes data/working_notes/research_arditi.md, so the full repo may cite the original (cites_only or discusses), but the text does not show this.

tranche.reason: The README makes no argument that any version is wrong, partial or needs restating. Its results are SAE feature-activation contrasts (102 features, 43 domain-specific) and a steering pass (8/8) with no rate of refusal. verdict_rules section 1 excludes steering effects with no behaviour rate and related-but-different constructs. From the text given it does not test the claim. If the full report (findings/rq1_poc_results.md, milestone_5 steering scores; not in the text) gives refusal rates under steering, it would be T2 on V4.
